findings.detail: The verifier's failure relies entirely on errexit. When a helper is sourced inside a condition, such as `if source "$entry" --base HEAD; then ...; fi`, Bash disables errexit throughout the sourced code. With snapshot A's inherited context and an external helper B, verification reports rejection but B continues loading its libraries. review-scope can then successfully emit scope data carrying A's identity. Sourced Bash invocation is explicitly supported by the new regression coverage. The same unchecked guard exists in both review-scope files and check-edit-worktree. This is a remaining instance of the recorded A1 executing-identity class.
findings.fix: Explicitly terminate on verifier failure, for example by appending `|| exit $?`, in all four Bash guards. Cover a rejected external caller sourced inside an if condition.
findings.title: write-bash-scripts: Checked commands: conditional sourcing ignores failed snapshot verification.

findings.detail: The wrapped command now includes snapshot verification, but every nonzero status still becomes codex_status and triggers the fallback prescribed at lines 15 and 91. If a snapshot member changes after bootstrap, the launcher refuses before Codex starts; the documented handler nevertheless directs review-anti-patterns and trim consumers to continue through their fallback using that bundle's references. Reporting the log does not prevent this continuation, which conflicts with helper-snapshots.md's requirement to stop after failed verification. This is a remaining instance of the recorded A3 instruction/control-flow class.
findings.fix: Distinguish launcher verification failures from failures after Codex starts. Make verification refusal terminal, and permit the existing fallback only for backend or reply failures after successful verification; regenerate the trim reference copies.
findings.title: Uncited: Snapshot-verification failures enter the ordinary Codex fallback path.

strengths: Snapshot refusals preserve stderr diagnostics and return nonzero.
Evidence consumers explicitly reject missing or mismatched producer provenance.
Snapshot creation refuses existing destinations rather than silently replacing them.
summary: Reviewed the full canonical committed scope against the captured literal base, including both maintained review-scope files. Two Important error-handling problems remain in the recorded executing-identity and instruction/control-flow classes. Runtime checks and plants were not run; stopped: recurring defect.
